events.title: The death of St. Louis IX on crusade
events.shortBlurb: The holy king of France died of disease in the crusader camp before the walls of Tunis…
body: In 1267 Louis took the cross a second time, and the expedition was steered toward North Africa: the emir of Tunis, Muhammad al-Mustansir, was reported ready to consider baptism, and the king's brother Charles of Anjou, newly master of Sicily, had designs of his own. Landing near Carthage in July 1270, the crusaders waited for Charles's fleet.

In the August heat dysentery swept the camp; the king's son John Tristan died in early August, and soon the king himself lay sick. He had himself laid on a bed of ashes strewn in the form of a cross, and died on 25 August, his last cries, says his confessor Geoffrey of Beaulieu, of Jerusalem. Charles's ships reached the camp that very day.

Two days later his son was proclaimed king as Philip III. The crusade dissolved: Charles made a profitable treaty with the emir in October and withdrew, while Edward of England, arriving too late, sailed on to Acre. Louis's heart was borne to Monreale and his bones to Saint-Denis; within a generation he was canonized.
